caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 509 of 2016
lawyer:
Khandaker Mahabub Hossain, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
For the Respondents ------ Not Represented
parties:
Siddiqur Rahman ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
S.M. Maola and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Surendra Kumar Sinha CJ. This petition is directed from a judgment of the High Court Division quashing the proceedings in C.R. Case No.15 of 2012 pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 3. Upon receipt of the complaint, the Magistrate got the complaint inquired into through Metropolitan Magistrate. The Magistrate holding inquiry examined 9 witnesses, and thereupon, by a lengthy order took cognizance of the offence. The accused persons thereupon moved the Metropolitan Sessions Judge. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge by a short order set aside the order of taking cognizance. The complainant then moved the High Court Division against the said order in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4215 of 2015. A Division Bench of the High Court Division summarily set aside the order of the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge on the reasoning that the Metropolitan Sessions Judge without affording the complainant any opportunity of being heard set aside the order. 

 4. Thereupon, the learned Sessions Judge heard the matter afresh and by judgment dated 19th June, 2012 set aside the order of taking cognizance. The complainant then moved the High Court Division. A Division Bench of the High Court Division quashed the proceedings. The High Court Division held that over the said incident a police case was instituted and the police after submission of charge-sheet the Druta Bichar Tribunal No. 2 is holding the trial of the case in Dhruta Bichar. Tribunal Case No.2 of 2010 in which 9 witnesses have been examined; that after three years of the occurrence, the complaint has been made, and that section 2051) would not be applicable in the case, inasmuch as, the learned Magistrate did not follow sub-section (1) of section 205D. 

 5. Admittedly over the said occurrence a police case was instituted in which 8 accused persons namely Md. Zahir alias Ripon, Haji Md. Monir Hossain, Abul Kashem, Rahmat Ullah, Samir, Parvez, Sharif Hossain and Din Islam are facing trial and in the complaint case, the complainant has implicated three accused persons namely S.M. Maola Reza, Md. Sohel and Noor Mohammad. This second set of accused persons are not involved in the police case. Therefore, we find that two sets of accused persons have been implicated over the killing of victim Hasan. The question involved in such eventually has been set at rest by the Supreme Court of Pakistan in Nur Elahi V, State, 18 DLR(SC) 474. It has been held that a fair procedure would be to proceed with both the cases by the same court, The trial court shall take up the complaint case first and it may call the witnesses mentioned in the police case if they were not already examined as court's witnesses under section 540A of the Code of Criminal Procedure so that they can be cross-examined by both set of accused persons. According to the Supreme Court, this procedure will enable the court to have the whole relevant evidence included in one trial and a decision could be arrived at after a proper consideration of the entire materials relied on by the parties. The accused persons would in addition obviously have the right to adduce defence witnesses if they so choose. It the trial results in a conviction it will be for the Public Prosecutor to consider whether or not he should withdraw from the prosecution, the accused persons involved in the police case. 

 6. To overcome the eventuality, the legislature came up with an amendment of the Code of Criminal Procedure by inserting section 205D and adding sub-section (3) of section 340. The Sessions Judge has noticed the case under reference and section 340, 205D but it failed to follow he ratio of the case referred to above and also the procedure provided in section 205D. 

 7. Section 205D provides that when a complaint is instituted, it is found to the Magistrate in course of inquiry or trial that an investigation by the police is in progress in relation to the offence which is the subject matter to inquiry or trial, the Magistrate shall stay the proceedings of such inquiry or trial and call for a report from the police officer conducting investigation. If the Magistrate finds that he has taken cognizance of the offence pursuant to a police report against any person who is in the complaint case, the Magistrate holding inquiry into the case shall try together the complaint case and the case arising out of the police report as if both the cases were instituted on a police report. However, if the police report does not relate to any accused in the complaint case or if the Magistrate does not take cognizance of any offence on the police report which shall proceed with the inquiry or trial of the complaint case. 

 8. I fail to understand why the High Court Division has misconstrued sub-section (3) of section 205D, which is applicable in this case. As mentioned above, the accused persons involved in the police case are not included in the complaint case, and therefore, the Magistrate is left with no option other than to hold the inquiry under sub-section (3) of section 2051) and upon such inquiry he finds prima-facie case against the accused persons and has taken cognizance of the offence. Non-performance of the procedures provided in sub-section (1) shall not be a legal ground to quash the proceeding, inasmuch as, there was no scope on his part to follow the said procedure since the complaint has been filed after the completion of the investigation. The trial of the case shall be held in accordance with sub-section (3) of section 205D. Since the trial of the police case has been undergoing, the trial of the complaint case shall be held simultaneously. There is no ambiguity in the provisions of law. More so, by addition of sub-section (3) of section 340, an accused person can now depose in support of his defence on oath in disproof of the charge made against him or any person charged together with him at the same time. When the case of Nur Elahi was considered, this provision was not in existence and accordingly, the Supreme Court of Pakistan gave the direction for holding trial of the complaint case first and also examination of the accused persons or some other persons as court's witnesses. In view of the legislative charge, there is no ambiguity in proceeding with the case. 

 9. The reasons assigned by the High Court Division that the learned Magistrate has not followed sub-section (1) of section 205D of the Code of Criminal Procedure and that there is delay of about 3 years in making the complaint are not legal grounds for quashing a proceeding. The Other reason assigned by the High Court Division is that 9 witnesses have been examined in the police case and at this belated stage, the trial of the accused persons is a sheer abuse of the process of the court is also not tenable in law. The procedure to be followed in this case is that the Druta Bichar Tribunal No. 2 shall hold simultaneous trial of the accused persons in the complaint case and shall dispose of the cases in accordance with sub-section (3) of section 2051) which is equally applicable to it shall conclude the trial of the police case first and postpone the delivery of the judgment till the trial of the complaint case is concluded and then it will decide which accused persons are involved in the killing of the victim and shall deliver judgment accordingly. If the court finds one set of accused persons or any one of them is involved in the killing it shall acquit the accused persons in the other case. The judgment of the learned Sessions Judge and the High Court Division are set aside. We direct the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate to transmit the case record to the Druta Bichar Tribunal No. 2 Dhaka for simultaneous trial of the case with Druta Bichar Tribunal Case No. 2 of 2010. The Dhruta Bichar Tribunal shall use the postmortem report and other alamats seized in the police case in this case also.
